cut its 2026 operating-margin outlook to no more than 1% after warning that a €6 billion ($6.9 billion) writedown on its 75% stake in Porsche
reflected weaker financial expectations for the luxury sports-car maker. The charge follows a €2.7 billion impairment last year.
decline highlights broader problems facing Volkswagen
, including weaker demand in China, pressure on its US business from tariffs and the costly transition to electric vehicles. Porsche
deliveries in China have fallen by more than half over the past four years, while sales have also weakened in North America and the Middle East, Africa and India region.
The brand’s margins, once significantly higher than those of the wider Volkswagen group

, have fallen below the group’s level and have been surpassed by budget marque Skoda. The Czech brand has effectively emerged as the more profitable operation within the group, according to independent autos analyst Matthias Schmidt.

Chief Executive Officer Michael Leiters said in an internal memo seen by Reuters that the company continues to target a medium-term operating margin of 10% to 15%. The company is also focusing on its highest-margin models under a “value over volume” strategy.
But shrinking sales volumes could limit the cash Porsche
undertakes its broader restructuring. The group is targeting a 9% operating margin by the end of the decade, compared with as much as 1% this year.
